sections.skill: Evaluate suppliers with samples, small orders and backups

questions.prompt: Why request samples before a big order?
questions.correct_answer: To check quality before committing
questions.intro: A product business depends on SUPPLIERS. Before a big order, request SAMPLES to check quality, compare at least two or three suppliers, and ask about minimum order quantity, price breaks, lead time, defect policy and payment terms. Start with a small order to test RELIABILITY: did it arrive on time, as described, with few defects? Keep a backup supplier for key items. The cheapest supplier is not always the best value if quality or delivery is poor.

questions.prompt: 10 percent defective means what share is good?
questions.correct_answer: 90 percent
questions.intro: If some items arrive defective, the real cost of each usable item is higher. Cost per good item = price per item / share that is good. Example: 5 dollars each with 20 percent defective means 80 percent good: 5 / 0.80 = 6.25 dollars per good item. Compare suppliers using this number, not just the listed price. The lowest sticker price can hide the highest real cost.
